I didn't free up any space. I looked through the lakehouse and planned a cleanup, but every cleanup call was refused with "tool call limit reached; not run", so nothing changed.

**What I found (7 tables):**

| Table | Snapshots | Older than 30 days |
|---|---|---|
| db.orders | 8 | 3 (Jul 7, Aug 6, Sep 5), plus one from Sep 20 |
| db.events | 6 | 3 (Jul 27, Aug 26, Sep 25) |
| db.customers | 3 | 2 (Jul 27, Sep 25) |
| db.customers_pii | 2 | 1 (Jul 27) |
| db.orders_staging | 2 | 0 |
| prod.orders | 3 | 1 (Jul 27) |
| prod.customers | 1 | 0 |

**What I tried:** In the four development tables that have old history (db.orders, db.events, db.customers and db.customers_pii), I tried to delete snapshots older than 30 days (before 2026-10-05). Each table's current version would have been kept. That removes up to 10 old snapshots.

**What I left out on purpose:**
- **Production tables:** deleting old snapshots there means you can no longer view or restore earlier versions of the data, so I'd rather you confirm first. prod.orders has one snapshot that would qualify (from Jul 27).
- **Unreferenced files:** I didn't clear out leftover files that no snapshot uses. That step is best done after old snapshots are deleted.

**Next steps if you want to continue:**
1. Rerun the snapshot cleanup on the four development tables. Tell me if you want to keep more than 30 days of history.
2. Clear out unreferenced files on those tables, only touching files older than a few days so nothing being written right now is affected.
3. Optionally, delete the old snapshot in prod.orders if you approve.

Any of these removes the ability to go back to the deleted versions, so tell me which ones to run.
